title: Reproduce the exact Ramsey number R(3,3)=6
statement: Show that every red/blue coloring of the unordered edges of K6 contains a monochromatic triangle, and exhibit a red/blue coloring of K5 without one. Produce an independently checkable finite certificate alongside a human-readable proof.
source_locator: DS1.18 section 2.1(a,d); Kiem–Pokutta–Spiegel section 1 identifies R(3,3)=6.
status_basis: Established theorem cited by the current dynamic survey and the inspected research paper. This is a proposed reproduction, not a new open problem.

title: Audit exact union-closed-family certificates on at most four elements
statement: Curator-proposed, pending peer assessment: enumerate every family F subseteq P({1,2,3,4}) with F nonempty, union(F) nonempty, and A union B in F for all A,B in F; for each eligible F record an element x in union(F) such that 2*|{A in F:x in A}| >= |F|. Deliver a completeness argument and an independently implemented verifier. Unused ground elements are allowed; repeated sets are not.
source_locator: Introduction for definitions; section 5 Theorem 17 for the already-known finite-case context.
status_basis: The four-element mathematical property is a special case of the source's reported twelve-element theorem. The certificate/benchmark packaging is a curator proposal; no claim of mathematical novelty or project execution.

title: Determine the four-color triangle Ramsey number R(3,3,3,3)
statement: Determine the least positive integer N such that every map from the unordered pairs of {1,...,N} to {1,2,3,4} gives some three distinct vertices whose three pair colors are equal.
source_locator: DS1.18 section 6.1.1, printed page 56 (PDF page index 55); Fettes–Kramer–Radziszowski abstract; Kiem–Pokutta–Spiegel section 2.
status_basis: The April 2026 author-maintained survey explicitly calls this open and states 51 <= N <= 62. Targeted October 2026 searches found no source establishing an exact value; the inspected recent-sounding multiplicity paper addresses a different quantity. This is a scoped literature check, not proof that no solution exists.

title: Determine the two-color Ramsey number R(5,5)
statement: Determine the least N such that every red/blue coloring of the edges of K_N has a monochromatic K5.
source_locator: DS1.18 section 2.1(e), printed page 8; Table Ib.
status_basis: The 2026 survey gives a gap and discusses a conjectured exact value. A separate current-status review remains outstanding.

title: Deterministic polynomial-time dense factorization over finite fields
statement: Given a degree-n dense univariate polynomial over a represented finite field F_q, find a deterministic factorization algorithm whose bit complexity is polynomial in n and log q; representation, preprocessing, and uniformity conventions require specification before a full card.
status_basis: The inspected AIM list labels the question open. Its date and all subsequent algorithmic results remain to be checked; no 2026 openness claim.

title: Sparse finite-field trinomial root decision
statement: For q a prime power, 0 < beta < alpha <= q-1, and a,b in F_q, decide whether x^alpha + a*x^beta + b has an F_q root in time polynomial in log q, with the field and sparse exponents explicitly encoded.
status_basis: Historical source explicitly asks this question. Current algorithms, randomized versus deterministic interpretations, and field representation costs are unverified.

title: Classify when polynomial convexity implies SOS-convexity
statement: For positive n and positive even degree d, classify when every convex real, nonhomogeneous n-variable polynomial of degree at most d has an SOS Hessian: Hessian(p)=M(x)^T M(x) for some real polynomial matrix M.
source_locator: Historical AIM report, 'Sum of Squares and Polynomial Convexity'; Ahmadi–Parrilo abstract, nonhomogeneous-polynomial characterization.
status_basis: The later paper characterizes equality by n=1, d=2, or (n,d)=(2,4). Retained as a status-correction example; the homogeneous-form version and exceptional case are distinct records.

title: A rational curve through a prescribed rational point on a K3 surface
statement: Given a K3 surface X over Q and x in X(Q), must there be a rational curve R contained in X, defined over Q, and containing x? The meaning of rational curve over Q versus geometrically rational curve must be reconciled with the problem's original context before promotion.
source_locator: Problem 10, final page, question attributed to Jean-Louis Colliot-Thélène.
status_basis: Directly recorded question in the inspected problem list. Neither the date nor later special/general cases have been audited; not a verified 2026 open status.

title: Construct an intersection-body polytope that is not a polar zonotope
statement: For dimensions n>5, construct a polytope K that is an intersection body but is not the polar body of a zonotope; confirm the source's symmetry, normalization, and definition of intersection body before treating this as an executable specification.
status_basis: Listed as a construction problem in the 2010 workshop notes. No current status audit has been completed.

title: Relate the Aubry set of a vector-field Lagrangian to chain recurrence
statement: Let M be a compact smooth manifold with a Riemannian metric and smooth vector field f, and let L(x,v)=0.5*||v-f(x)||^2. Characterize the projection to M of the zero-cohomology Aubry set using the dynamics of the flow of f; specifically, does this projection contain the chain recurrent set?
source_locator: Chapter A, problem 1, attributed to Albert Fathi; printed page 3.
status_basis: The projected formulation agrees with Fathi–Figalli–Rifford's later statement. Their Theorem 1.6 settles smooth compact connected manifolds of dimensions at most three. The arbitrary-dimensional question and any more recent general results remain unverified.

title: Reproduce Huang's hypercube degree theorem
statement: Reconstruct a proof that every induced subgraph on 2^(n-1)+1 vertices of the n-dimensional hypercube has maximum degree at least sqrt(n), for every integer n >= 1.
status_basis: Huang's proof is explicit; the 2012 open-list entry is superseded. Reproduction is calibration, not a new solution.

title: Audit finite-sample split likelihood-ratio coverage in a Bernoulli model
statement: Specialize universal inference to iid Bernoulli(p), a prespecified split of 20 observations into two groups of 10, training estimator q=(K1+1)/12, and alpha=1/20. Reproduce the all-p coverage proof and exact rejection probabilities on p in {1/10,...,9/10}.
source_locator: SRC-FORMAL-003, Section 2, Theorem 1; finite parameters chosen for calibration
status_basis: The guarantee follows from the published theorem under its assumptions. The finite Bernoulli benchmark is a curator-selected reproduction protocol; no calculation has been run.

title: Build a bounded exact copy-lemma certificate census
statement: For five original finite random variables X1,...,X5 and one conditional copy X6 of X1 over (X2,X3), enumerate sums of at most three distinct elemental six-variable Shannon inequalities, each with coefficient 1 or 2. Use exactly the four marginal entropy equalities H(6,S)=H(1,S) for S subset of {2,3}, including the empty set, and I(6;1,4,5|2,3)=0. Determine which sums eliminate all coordinates involving X6 after adding rational combinations of those five equality rows; retain exact certificates and canonical projected inequalities.
source_locator: SRC-FORMAL-004, Section 6, Definition 24 and Lemma 27 (full copy and restriction), Section 6.3 Claims 31-32, and Problem 6; bounded protocol is curator-proposed
status_basis: The copy-lemma encoding is supported by Csirmaz's Definition 24 and Lemma 27. The finite three-row, coefficient-{1,2} search is curator-proposed; neither its novelty nor its ability to yield a non-Shannon consequence has been established. The two-variable conditioning avoids the singleton obstruction only.

title: Classify entropic and almost-entropic extremal rays of the five-variable Shannon cone
statement: Determine which extremal rays of the five-variable Shannon cone contain entropic points and which are almost entropic; preserve the distinction between membership and closure.
status_basis: The 2025 survey poses it and the inspected 2026 paper still identifies unresolved rays. No exhaustive post-March-2026 resolution check.

title: Compare maximum-entropy and iterated copy-lemma inequality methods
statement: Decide whether a single MEM or GMEM application proves a valid entropy inequality unavailable to every iterated copy-lemma derivation, and whether the converse separation exists.
status_basis: The survey explicitly asks both directions. The 2026 construction is related progress, not evidence of method equivalence or separation; later status remains to check.

title: Fourier entropy–influence conjecture
statement: Is there a universal C such that every Boolean f on the uniform discrete cube satisfies sum_S fhat(S)^2 log2(1/fhat(S)^2) <= C sum_S |S| fhat(S)^2, with zero summands interpreted as zero?
source_locator: Named FEI entry in SRC-FORMAL-005; SRC-FORMAL-013 Section 1.1
status_basis: A 2025 primary-paper revision still treats this as a conjecture. Search found bounds, not an inspected complete proof; current open status is not exhaustively certified.

title: Mansour's Fourier concentration conjecture for DNF
statement: For Boolean f represented by a DNF with s>1 terms and epsilon in (0,1/2], does some collection of at most s^(O(log(1/epsilon))) Fourier coefficients carry at least 1-epsilon of squared Fourier mass?
status_basis: Exact strong statement comes from the 2012 collection; the 2025 paper discusses related consequences. No complete modern status audit; do not merge the strong statement with weaker constant-epsilon variants.

title: Tomaszewski's variance-one signed-sum bound
statement: For independent uniform signs epsilon_i and real coefficients with sum_i a_i^2=1, reproduce selected proof components of P(|sum_i a_i epsilon_i| <= 1) >= 1/2.
status_basis: Keller and Klein prove the bound; the 2012 list's open label is obsolete. Full proof reproduction is substantial and is not scheduled.

title: Existence of a binary q-Fano plane
statement: Does there exist a set of 3-dimensional subspaces of F_2^7 such that every 2-dimensional subspace lies in exactly one selected 3-dimensional subspace?
status_basis: The 2013 problem is explicit. Later search surfaced restrictions on automorphisms but those papers were not fully incorporated; no 2026 openness certification. Search-space size prevents an easy-AI label.

title: Deterministic polynomial-time identity testing for general arithmetic circuits
statement: Does a uniform deterministic Turing machine decide whether a division-free arithmetic circuit over Q computes the zero polynomial in time poly(s,n,d,L), where s counts gates and wires, n counts commuting variables, L is the total binary encoding length of the rational constants, and d bounds the circuit formal degree? Require d to be bounded by a fixed polynomial in the full input encoding length. The target is polynomial bit complexity; a count of unit-cost rational operations is insufficient.
source_locator: SRC-FORMAL-007 introduction and section 5; SRC-IMPACT-011 introduction, theorems 1.1-1.2 and definitions 2.1-2.2; SRC-IMPACT-012 corollary 2.7; SRC-IMPACT-013 introduction and theorem 1. SRC-IMPACT-014 definitions 2.2.1 and 2.2.6, theorem 2.2.8 and section 2.6; SRC-IMPACT-015 section 1.1.
status_basis: The 2026 bounded-read paper identifies general deterministic PIT as open. The cited complexity references specify the formal-degree and bit-encoding conventions used here. Later restricted-model improvements were inspected; no resolution of this polynomial-formal-degree, commutative bit-complexity target was located in the scoped search.

title: Reconstruct the stable Ramsey omega-model separation
statement: Reconstruct the theorem that an omega-model of RCA_0 + SRT^2_2 need not satisfy RT^2_2, preserving the standard first-order part and the chosen second-order sets.
status_basis: The author-hosted proof gives the separation; this is a theorem-reproduction option, not an unsolved implication.

title: Characterize admissible e-processes
statement: For a precisely fixed null distribution class and filtration, characterize e-process admissibility by matching necessary and sufficient conditions under the pointwise domination order used in the source.
status_basis: The 2023 survey reports a gap. This candidate is a source-level general question; a tractable class and modern status review are prerequisites to a full card.

title: Reproduce the CHSH optimum with an exact certificate
statement: For a bipartite quantum state and local Hermitian observables A0,A1,B0,B1 with eigenvalues in {-1,+1}, reproduce the universal bound |<A0 tensor B0>+<A0 tensor B1>+<A1 tensor B0>-<A1 tensor B1>| <= 2 sqrt(2), including an attaining realization and an exact upper-bound certificate.
status_basis: The inspected source supplies a proof and attaining certificate. The project proposes a reproduction task, not a new bound.

title: Certify deficiency-zero hypotheses for small reaction networks
statement: For a finite supplied network of mass-action reactions, compute delta = number_of_complexes - number_of_linkage_classes - rank(stoichiometric_matrix), test weak reversibility, and issue a traceable applicability certificate for the deficiency-zero theorem. Begin with at most four species, six complexes and ten reactions; these limits are curator chosen.
source_locator: ACK Definitions 2.1-2.4 and Theorem 3.1; Baez theorem
status_basis: The theorem and hypotheses are verified in the opened sources. The finite input limits and certificate task are curator-designed calibration work.

title: Enumerate equilibria of a supplied rational bimatrix game
statement: Given rational m by n payoff matrices with m,n <= 3 and a certified nondegeneracy assumption, reproduce support enumeration and output every Nash equilibrium with exact best-response certificates. Degenerate inputs must be flagged for a separate full-set treatment.
source_locator: von Stengel Section 2, Definition 2, Propositions 1 and 3, Algorithm 4; Section 7
status_basis: The opened author survey gives support enumeration and explains its nondegeneracy requirement. The <=3 restriction is a curator-selected calibration scope.

title: Yang-Mills existence and a mass gap in four dimensions
statement: Construct a nontrivial quantum Yang-Mills theory on R^4 for any compact simple gauge group G, satisfying the axiomatic requirements of the official statement, and prove a positive mass gap.
source_locator: Jaffe-Witten Section 4, PDF p.6; Clay current Unsolved label
status_basis: The current institutional page explicitly reports unsolved status. No independent survey of all claimed proofs or feasible decomposition has been completed.

title: NPT bound entanglement
statement: Determine whether a finite-dimensional bipartite entangled quantum state can have negative partial transpose while remaining undistillable under LOCC for every finite number of copies.
source_locator: PRX Quantum Problem 4; Fu–Gao–Park v3, introduction and section 4; Wu–Zou v1, section 1.1 and Discussion; Zenodo qutrit candidate description.
status_basis: The inspected 2026 papers retain the all-copy NPT bound-entanglement question. Two-copy solution claims, three-copy sector results and an unreviewed d=3 three-copy candidate do not settle it. A focused update search on 2026-10-20 found no resolution of the stated all-copy target; this is not an exhaustive search or independent proof review.

title: Two-copy distillability of the two-ququart Werner boundary state
statement: Determine whether rho(4,-1/2) = (I - F/2)/(16 - 2), with F the swap on C^4 tensor C^4, is two-copy distillable.
source_locator: PRX Quantum Problem 5 and equation (5), PDF pp.8-9; arXiv:2607.24309 abstract
status_basis: Three inspected 2026 preprints claim two-copy undistillability of this exact state. Theorem 1.1 of Fu–Gao–Park v3 and Corollary B of Fraser–Huber–Pozsgay–Vona match the original parameters. The entry remains unverified pending independent proof review and specialist assessment of the recent claims; it must not be offered as an ordinary open target.

title: Four mutually unbiased bases in dimension six
statement: Construct four orthonormal bases of C^6 for which squared inner products between vectors in different bases all equal 1/6. This is the construction alternative explicitly included in the source's Problem 2.
status_basis: The 2022 review states the task. No comprehensive 2023-2026 status check was performed. Numerical near-solutions do not certify existence.

title: Audit uniform coordinate scaling in an exchange functional
statement: For a supplied analytic exchange-functional expression and n_gamma(r)=gamma^3 n(gamma r), gamma>0, derive whether E_x[n_gamma]=gamma E_x[n] on an explicitly stated density class; report missing regularity or integrability assumptions.
status_basis: The scaling property is a stated exact constraint. The supplied-expression audit is curator-proposed reproduction, not an open general DFT problem.

title: Separate finite SIS absorption from approximate endemic equilibria
statement: For a supplied connected simple graph with 2-6 vertices, positive rational transmission and recovery rates and no importation, construct the finite continuous-time SIS generator, verify its absorbing disease-free state, and explain why this does not imply equivalence to an endemic fixed point of a mean-field approximation.
source_locator: Review Section II absorbing-state discussion; IV.A Markov approach
status_basis: The review explicitly distinguishes finite-system absorption and thermodynamic-limit or metastable concepts. Graph-size bound is curator chosen.

title: Reproduce equilibrium branches in an energy-balance climate model
statement: For the deterministic energy-balance model of Ashwin and von der Heydt, use the decimal parameter values in Table 1 as exact model inputs on T in [260,310] K. Reproduce Gamma(T) in equation (18), isolate every root of R'(T) in this interval with certified error control, classify nondegenerate folds and regular equilibrium stability, and verify S=1/R'(T) wherever R'(T)≠0. State why this local sensitivity formula does not apply at a fold. Noise is set to zero and carbon dioxide is a fixed positive parameter.
source_locator: Section 3, equations (15)–(21), Table 1 and Figure 2; Table 1 is on printed p.1540.
status_basis: The paper supplies the illustrative model and equilibrium analysis. The temperature interval and certification requirements make the existing reproduction target precise; they do not define a real-world climate threshold.

title: Characterize observational equivalence in small biological ODE models
statement: For a future reviewer-selected family of at most three polynomial ODEs with a declared observable and input protocol, determine parameter transformations that preserve the ideal noise-free output and distinguish these from practical non-identifiability under noisy samples.
status_basis: The sources motivate this curator-proposed direction but do not pose the bounded task. The model and novelty baseline remain unspecified, so there is no literature-open claim to confirm.

title: Reproduce a product-form stationary distribution on a conserved reaction class
statement: For a small mass-action network with a supplied positive complex-balanced equilibrium and an explicitly specified finite closed irreducible state class, normalize the ACK product-form weights on that class and verify the stationary master equation exactly.
status_basis: Primary paper establishes the product-form result. Conditional restriction to a conserved class is essential; the task does not claim unconditional independence of species counts.

title: Reconstruct the assumptions of the cosmological-constant no-go argument
statement: Reproduce the logical steps of the Weinberg self-adjustment no-go argument as presented in Padilla Section 3.2, with an assumption ledger; identify which hypotheses a supplied proposed evasion explicitly relaxes.
status_basis: Source presents an existing no-go argument. The audit is curator-designed and does not show that any proposal resolves the cosmological-constant problem or matches observations.

title: Bound structural perturbations in a selected biological model
statement: For a reviewer-selected small reaction-network model, enumerate single-reaction additions or removals within a declared species and stoichiometry bound; classify which preserve a specifically chosen invariant or steady-state property.
source_locator: Vittadello-Stumpf Section 3.3 topological sensitivity and Section 3.4 design principles
status_basis: The sources motivate this curator-proposed direction but do not pose the bounded task. The model and novelty baseline remain unspecified, so there is no literature-open claim to confirm.

title: Exact finite satisfiability for a small monadic fragment
statement: For a closed, equality-free first-order formula with k <= 3 unary predicates, no functions or constants, at most 40 syntax-tree nodes and quantifier nesting at most 4, decide satisfiability over nonempty finite domains. Reproduce the predicate-type reduction to nonempty subsets of {0,1}^k, then return a satisfying model or an exhaustive rejection certificate. The size limits are curator-defined calibration conditions.
source_locator: SRC-MATH-101, Section 5.1, Lemmas 36 and 38 (printed p. 17); Section 2.4 and Definition 14 fix the logical setting.
status_basis: The source proves decidability for a broader unary-predicate fragment. The bounded certificate task is an editorial specialization of that known result.

title: Exact mixing certificates for small positive Markov chains
statement: Given a rational row-stochastic matrix P of order 2 <= n <= 6 with every entry positive and every reduced denominator at most 100, compute its stationary probability row vector pi and tau = max_(i,j) (1/2) sum_k |P_ik-P_jk|. Certify d(t) = max_i ||P^t(i,.)-pi||_TV <= tau^t for every integer t >= 1, and return an integer T >= 1 with tau^T <= 1/100. Supply exact row-coupling certificates and a general argument, not only sampled trajectories.
status_basis: The cited textbook gives the coupling and submultiplicativity facts from which the stated certificate follows. Matrix-size, denominator and tolerance limits are curator-defined calibration conditions.

title: Transfer-matrix calibration for the one-dimensional Ising model
statement: For N >= 3 periodic spins s_i in {-1,+1}, finite beta >= 0 and real h, define Z_N = sum_s exp(beta sum_(i=1)^N s_i s_(i+1) + h sum_(i=1)^N s_i), with s_(N+1)=s_1. Reproduce the transfer-matrix formula for Z_N and prove that psi(beta,h) = lim_(N->infinity) N^-1 log Z_N exists and is real-analytic in h for each finite beta. Here beta and h are dimensionless parameters; the task concerns this nearest-neighbor model.
source_locator: SRC-MATH-103, Section 3.3, Theorem 3.9 and proof, equations (3.10)-(3.11), pp. 90-92.
status_basis: The theorem and its transfer-matrix proof are present in the inspected author chapter. Reproducing them would be calibration, not a new model solution.

title: Quadratic generation of matroid toric ideals: the weak White conjecture
statement: For every finite matroid M of positive rank on [n], with set of bases B(M), let phi: Q[y_B : B in B(M)] -> Q[x_1,...,x_n] send y_B to the product of x_i for i in B. Is ker(phi) generated by homogeneous quadratic binomials? All quadratic binomials preserving element multiplicities are allowed; the claim does not require symmetric-exchange generators or a quadratic Gröbner basis.
source_locator: SRC-MATH-104, Conjecture 1.1(3) and its toric-ideal interpretation; SRC-MATH-105, Conjecture 1.1.
status_basis: The June 2026 source explicitly states quadratic generation as a conjecture. The July 2026 source separates it from the symmetric-exchange version it disproves and reports no counterexample to this weak version. A targeted update search found no later resolution, which is not proof of global open status.

title: Dirichlet interval eigenfunctions and completeness
statement: Reproduce the eigenvalues (n*pi)^2 and normalized eigenfunctions sqrt(2) sin(n*pi*x), n >= 1, for -u'' on [0,1] with u(0)=u(1)=0. Prove their completeness in L^2([0,1]) and state separately sufficient regularity and the Dirichlet boundary compatibility f(0)=f(1)=0 for uniform convergence on [0,1]; finite numerical eigenvalue agreement is insufficient.
source_locator: SRC-MATH-106, Section 5.4, Theorem 5.11 and the example on pp. 163-164.
status_basis: The source states the eigenpairs and integral-norm convergence for continuous functions; the L^2 completion and the chosen operator domain should be made explicit in a full card.

title: Discrete Gauss-Bonnet on a closed triangular surface
statement: For a finite connected closed orientable triangular simplicial surface with nondegenerate Euclidean faces, set d(v)=2*pi-sum_(f incident to v) angle_f(v). Prove sum_v d(v)=2*pi*(|V|-|E|+|F|). A computational illustration must also check the closed-manifold incidence conditions; a mesh with boundary requires a different boundary contribution.
status_basis: The inspected notes state the discrete identity. The candidate makes the closed-surface assumption explicit to avoid applying that formula to meshes with boundary.

title: Independent audit of the Fano quadratic-Gröbner obstruction
statement: Curator-proposed, pending review: independently reconstruct the Fano-matroid base-polytope encoding used in SRC-MATH-105 and check the claimed unsatisfiability certificate excluding a regular unimodular flag triangulation. Audit the correspondence to the assertion that its toric ideal has no quadratic Gröbner basis. This is a reproduction and statement-alignment task, not a search for an unresolved counterexample.
source_locator: SRC-MATH-105, Question 1.2, Theorem 3.1 and Section 4.1, especially its formal statements and cvc5 subsection.
status_basis: The published preprint statement and certificate description match this curator-proposed independent audit. Reading them does not complete the audit: the solver artifact and mathematical equivalence have not been checked. The underlying Gröbner-basis negative claim is distinct from White's weaker quadratic-generation conjecture.

title: Check common quadratic Lyapunov certificates for small matrix polytopes
statement: Given 1-4 rational matrices A_i of a common dimension d <= 4, a rational symmetric P, and rational alpha > 0, verify exactly that P and every residual -(A_i^T P + P A_i + 2 alpha P) are positive definite. If accepted, supply the conditional exponential-decay certificate for xdot = A(t)x with arbitrary measurable A(t) in their convex hull. Rejection does not imply instability. The input bounds and strict-residual convention define a curator-proposed calibration.
source_locator: Boyd et al., Section 5.1, equations (5.8) and (5.17)
status_basis: The common-quadratic criterion and decay implication are established in the opened monograph. This task checks supplied witnesses, without claiming a new theorem or complete stability decision procedure.

title: Verify the equal-block language of a locally constrained tree-adjoining grammar
statement: Reproduce the nonempty string-language claim in Vijay-Shankar and Joshi, Example 2.5: the locally constrained TAG generates exactly a^n b^n c^n for integers n >= 1 when empty yields are excluded. Transcribe its elementary trees, preserve null-adjoining restrictions at auxiliary roots and feet, prove both language inclusions, and provide derivations for n = 1,...,6. Record separately whether the initial tree admits the empty word. The finite example range is curator chosen.
status_basis: The source presents the equal-block construction with local adjoining constraints. This reproduces that construction, not an unrestricted-TAG claim or an empirical claim about language.

title: Check twisted-state spectra on Kuramoto cycle networks
domain: Dynamics on networks and collective behavior
statement: For the simple undirected cycle C_n, n >= 3, consider theta_dot_j = sin(theta_(j-1)-theta_j) + sin(theta_(j+1)-theta_j), with indices modulo n and phases modulo 2 pi. Reproduce the equilibrium and Jacobian spectrum for theta_j = 2 pi q j/n, 0 <= q <= floor(n/2), and classify linear stability modulo uniform rotation. Build an exact sign table only for 3 <= n <= 20. Extra zero eigenvalues must be labeled inconclusive for nonlinear stability. The finite range is curator chosen.
source_locator: Townsend et al., equations (4)-(5) and Section II.1; McRae, Section 1.2
status_basis: The spectrum is a known result in the opened paper. Later work preserves the distinction between second-order criticality and nonlinear stability. No table or simulation has been produced by this project.

title: Determine the sharp connectivity threshold for homogeneous Kuramoto synchronization
domain: Dynamics on networks and collective behavior
statement: For finite simple undirected graphs with identical natural frequencies and unit positive edge coupling, let mu_c be the infimum of thresholds guaranteeing convergence to the all-in-phase state from almost every initial phase configuration whenever minimum degree/(n-1) exceeds the threshold. Determine whether mu_c = 3/4. This concerns nonlinear almost-everywhere global synchronization, not merely the absence of positive eigenvalues at selected equilibria.
source_locator: Kassabov et al., abstract and Sections I, VI; McRae (2026 v2), Section 3.4.3
status_basis: The 2021 paper proves the upper bound; the August 2026 follow-up still calls sharpness conjectural. Targeted later-work searches found no resolution. This is a dated source-supported status, not an exhaustive novelty audit. No historical lower bound is asserted as current.

title: Reproduce front-door identification in a latent-confounded mediator graph
statement: For a finite-valued acyclic structural causal model with observed X, M, Y, latent U, and only arrows U->X, U->Y, X->M, M->Y, derive P(y | do(X=x)) = sum_m P(m | x) sum_xprime P(y | m,xprime) P(xprime). Assume independent exogenous disturbances, well-defined interventions and strictly positive relevant observed probabilities. Identify assumptions at each step and distinguish identification from estimation or empirical confirmation of the graph.
source_locator: Wu and Robeva, Figure 1(b) and Theorem 2.5
status_basis: The opened 2026 paper restates Pearl's classical sufficient criterion and formula. This is a calibration on the classical graph; the criterion is not claimed necessary and the graph is not inferred from observations.

title: Reproduce the LRU paging competitive bound with explicit initial-state terms
statement: In uniform-cost demand paging with cache capacity k >= 1, reproduce the equal-capacity specialization of Sleator and Tarjan's Theorem 6: LRU incurs at most k times the optimal offline fault count plus a constant depending only on initial cache states. Specify a common initially empty convention and derive its startup term rather than assume it vanishes. Explain why finite trace tests do not prove the all-sequence guarantee.
source_locator: Section 4, Theorem 6 and following initial-cache discussion
status_basis: The primary paper proves the cache-size-dependent bound and discusses its additive initial-state term. This is an established-result calibration, not a guarantee for other paging models.

title: Reproduce exact Moran fixation probabilities
statement: For a well-mixed Moran population of N=20 individuals, with no mutation and constant relative mutant fitness r in {1/2,1,2}, compute the probability that a single mutant reaches fixation before extinction. At each discrete update, choose a reproducing individual proportional to fitness and independently choose a uniformly random individual for replacement, including the reproducer. Use exact arithmetic to solve the absorbing-chain equations and reproduce u_1=(1-r^(-1))/(1-r^(-20)) for r≠1 and u_1=1/20 for r=1.
source_locator: McCandlish et al., equation (1) and Section 2; Adlam and Nowak, Introduction and equation (1).
status_basis: The sources give the known formula and update rule. The population size, fitness values and exact-arithmetic deliverable are curator-selected calibration conditions.

title: Recover the linear stability threshold of triangular Lagrange points
statement: In the planar circular restricted three-body problem with unit primary separation, unit angular speed and mass fractions 1−mu and mu, 0<mu≤1/2, reproduce the linearized characteristic polynomial at L4 and L5: lambda^4+lambda^2+(27/4)mu(1−mu). Establish bounded solutions of the linearized system for 0<mu<mu_R and linear instability for mu_R<mu≤1/2, where mu_R=(1−sqrt(23/27))/2. Exclude mu=mu_R, and do not claim nonlinear stability.
source_locator: Fitzpatrick, Stability of Lagrange points, equations (9.73)–(9.88); Co-rotating frame, equations (9.22)–(9.30).
status_basis: The author text provides the characteristic equation and mass criterion. The card explicitly restricts their interpretation to the nondegenerate linearized planar problem.

title: Verify the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck transition law and equilibrium
statement: For the one-dimensional Itô process dX_t=−a X_t dt+sqrt(2D)dW_t, with a,D>0 and deterministic X_0=x_0, reproduce the Gaussian transition law with mean x_0 exp(−at) and variance (D/a)(1−exp(−2at)). Verify its Fokker–Planck equation, normalization, weak initial limit, Gaussian composition law and stationary density proportional to exp(−a x^2/(2D)). Check zero stationary probability current and detailed balance.
source_locator: Bazant lecture 14, pp.4–5 and Appendix A.1–A.2, pp.7–8; Tong, Section 3.2.2, equations (3.28)–(3.31).
status_basis: The transition and equilibrium formulas are established results in the cited lectures. The verification checklist is a curator-selected calibration task.

title: Reproduce log-concavity of Moran fixation probability

status_basis: The cited paper proves log-concavity; this is a symbolic reproduction task with no novelty claim.

title: Verify Jacobi conservation and certified forbidden regions
statement: For the planar circular restricted three-body model with mu=1/100 and unit separation and angular speed, verify conservation of J=2Omega−(x_dot^2+y_dot^2) along smooth collision-free solutions, where Omega=(x^2+y^2)/2+(1−mu)/r_1+mu/r_2, and r_1 and r_2 are distances to the primaries at (−mu,0) and (1−mu,0). At J=16/5, classify the 1/20-by-1/20 closed grid boxes covering [-2,2]^2 as wholly forbidden only if a rigorous upper bound for 2Omega is below J. For every box not containing a primary, report a rigorous finite upper bound for 2Omega and the enclosure method. Mark boxes containing a primary or whose upper bound is not below J as undecided. This is a pointwise exclusion certificate, not an orbit-reachability or topology claim.
status_basis: The conservation law and necessary accessibility inequality are established in the source. The finite box grid, mass ratio and energy are curator-selected calibration parameters.

title: Verify equilibrium for an overdamped quartic potential
statement: For the dimensionless overdamped diffusion dX_t=−m V'(X_t)dt+sqrt(2m theta)dW_t on the real line, with m,theta>0 and V(x)=(x^2−1)^2/4, verify that p_eq(x)=Z^(-1)exp(−V(x)/theta) is normalizable and has zero stationary probability current. source_locator: Bazant lecture 14, p.4, probability current and Boltzmann formula; Tong, equations (3.28)–(3.31).
status_basis: The equilibrium relation is known. Applying it to this confining quartic potential is a curator-selected calibration, not an open chemistry problem.

status_basis: The source supplies the model and linear instability criterion. The parameter pair and one-dimensional interval are curator-selected; nonlinear outcomes and empirical morphogenesis are not assessed.

title: Complete EFX for four additive goods agents
statement: For four agents and every finite set M of indivisible goods with nonnegative additive values v_i, does there exist a complete partition X of M such that v_i(X_i)≥v_i(X_j\{g}) for all agents i,j and every g∈X_j? The deletion quantifier includes goods of zero value to i (EFX0).

Empty bundles impose no deletion comparison. No Pareto-optimality condition is required.

source_locator: He and Tao, Section 6; Zhang, Definition 1 and Section 6; Evidence Press, verification status.

source_locator: Jin and Tao, Sections 2-5; He and Tao, Section 6; Lin, Wu and Zhou, Theorem 3.5 and Example 3.6.

status_basis: The April 2026 journal article explicitly calls this classical conjecture unsolved. The scoped search did not establish a general resolution. Counterexamples to uniform variants have different quantifiers and do not decide this statement.

title: The Birkhoff caustic-integrability conjecture

status_basis: The 2026 journal abstract explicitly says the caustic-integrability conjecture remains open, even for algebraic ovals. The polynomial-first-integral theorem has additional assumptions and is not a resolution of this statement.

title: The sharp asymptotic Littlewood inequality for exponential sums
statement: Uniformly over n-element A⊂Z, is ∫₀¹|∑_{a∈A} exp(2πiat)|dt ≥ (4/π²−o(1))log n as n→∞?

status_basis: The December 2025 author revision explicitly calls the strong conjecture unresolved. A scoped 2026 search found related work on inverse formulations but did not establish this sharp lower bound.

title: Unconditional polynomial-time derandomization: BPP versus P

source_locator: Wigderson, Conjecture 7.8; Doron et al., section 1.1.
status_basis: Recent generator results remain conditional. The scoped later-literature search found no unconditional resolution.

title: Deterministic logarithmic space for directed reachability: L versus NL
statement: Can directed s–t reachability be decided in deterministic O(log n) work space? This is equivalent to L=NL.
status_basis: The source presents L versus NL as open. The later search found no resolution of directed reachability; randomized-space claims are different.

title: Superpolynomial Boolean circuit lower bounds for NP

source_locator: Wigderson, Conjecture 5.4; Lu et al., section 1.3 discussion of SAT circuit lower-bound formulas.
status_basis: The 2026 proof-complexity paper continues to treat the SAT circuit lower bound as unknown.

source_locator: Wigderson, section 5.2.1, discussion immediately following Open Problem 5.8.
status_basis: Source-reported open; later searches did not identify a resolution for this unrestricted gate model.

title: A superpolynomial gap between Boolean circuits and formulas

source_locator: Wigderson, section 5.2.2; Lu et al., section 1.1 comparison of circuit and proof lower bounds.
status_basis: Source-reported open; inspected restricted-model and proof-complexity advances do not establish this separation.

title: Valiant's VP versus VNP over the rational numbers
statement: Is VP_Q different from VNP_Q? Equivalently, must the permanent family require superpolynomial-size arithmetic circuits over Q?
source_locator: Wigderson, Conjecture 12.21; Narayanan, abstract and introduction.
status_basis: The July 2026 paper gives restricted-depth progress and explicitly leaves the elusive-function parameters for full separation unavailable.

title: Polynomial-time graph isomorphism
statement: Is there a deterministic algorithm polynomial in the input size that decides whether two finite simple graphs are isomorphic?
status_basis: The August 2026 source still describes quasipolynomial general algorithms and unsolved bottlenecks.

title: Polynomial-time tournament isomorphism
statement: Can isomorphism of arbitrary finite tournaments be decided deterministically in polynomial time?
source_locator: Raßmann–Schweitzer, abstract and introduction, paragraph beginning 'Nevertheless'.
status_basis: The 2026 paper solves bounded-VC and bounded-chromatic tournament classes, while retaining the unrestricted target.

title: Polynomial-time isomorphism for multiplication-table groups
statement: Given two finite groups by complete multiplication tables, decide isomorphism in deterministic time polynomial in the table length.
source_locator: Raßmann–Schweitzer, opening introduction on the two isomorphism bottlenecks.
status_basis: The current source identifies this verbose-input group problem as an unresolved bottleneck.

title: NP-completeness of ordinary MCSP under deterministic many-one reductions
statement: Is the ordinary Minimum Circuit Size Problem NP-complete under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions? Input is a complete Boolean truth table and a gate bound s; ask whether a circuit of size at most s computes the table.
status_basis: 2025–2026 conditional, quasipolynomial, randomized and implicit-variant results do not prove this exact completeness statement.

title: A strongly polynomial algorithm for general linear programming
statement: Does rational linear programming admit an algorithm with a number of arithmetic operations polynomial only in the numbers of variables and constraints, and with all intermediate encodings polynomial in the input length?
status_basis: The survey explicitly reports the general problem open. Later searches found strongly polynomial restricted LP/MDP results, not the general algorithm.

title: Superpolynomial lower bounds for unrestricted Frege proofs
statement: Exhibit an explicit family of propositional tautologies whose shortest Frege proofs have superpolynomial total symbol size in the tautology length.
status_basis: The 2026 source describes strong proof-system lower bounds as unresolved; non-tautologies with no proofs do not qualify.

title: Superpolynomial AC0[2]-Frege lower bounds for known tautologies
statement: Find an explicit tautology family requiring superpolynomial-size AC0[2]-Frege proofs at every fixed proof depth, where proof lines may use unbounded-fan-in AND, OR and parity gates.
source_locator: Lu et al., section 1.1 and discussion in section 1.3.
status_basis: The 2026 DNF construction excludes easy proofs but leaves tautologicity open; it therefore does not solve this task.

title: Constant-depth IPS lower bounds for unsatisfiable CNF families
statement: Exhibit an explicit unsatisfiable CNF family whose standard clause-polynomial and Boolean-axiom encoding requires superpolynomial-size constant-depth Ideal Proof System certificates over Q. An IPS certificate C(x,y) satisfies C(x,0)=0 and C(x,F(x))=1.
source_locator: Lu et al., section 1.2 and Theorem 16.
status_basis: The source explicitly distinguishes this unresolved propositional task from lower bounds for purely algebraic instances.

status_basis: The February 2026 source poses the unrelativized question as open and proves oracle barriers.

source_locator: Egidy, introduction question Q2 and section 1.2.2.
status_basis: Oracle worlds giving different answers do not settle the ordinary unrelativized question.

title: Linear-size sample compression for every binary VC class
statement: Does every binary concept class of finite VC dimension d admit an exact realizable compression scheme storing O(d) original labeled examples plus auxiliary bits, counted together, from which a predictor consistent with the entire sample is reconstructed?

status_basis: The 2025 source reports the conjecture open. A 2026 apparent solution was checked against the current withdrawn record, which identifies an incorrect proof.

source_locator: Servedio, section 3.1; Moakahr et al., abstract and sections 1.3 and 7.
status_basis: The 2026 product-distribution analysis does not settle this unrestricted distribution-free target.

status_basis: The survey identifies polynomial learning of log(n)-juntas as a prerequisite for broader learning goals; the later search found only restricted-distribution progress.

title: Polynomial-time learning parity with constant random classification noise

status_basis: The June 2026 source explicitly reports the conjecture open and describes progress on hypothetical counterexamples.

status_basis: The current source describes the four-variable structure as largely unknown; its five-variable method does not supply a complete characterization.

status_basis: The 2025 paper explicitly leaves this target open. Searches for the title and subsequent conjecture resolutions found no settling source; this negative search is limited.

T counts all updates until consensus.
status_basis: The 2025 paper explicitly leaves this target open. Searches for the title and subsequent conjecture resolutions found no settling source; this negative search is limited.

statement: Set x'=x exp(alpha−u^2/2−c0 x), u'=(1−s)u−c1 s x, with 0<alpha<1, c0>0, c1≠0 and 0<s<1. status_basis: Conjecture 1 explicitly proposes extending the theorem to slower positive evolution. A title/author/conjecture search through the assessment date found no resolution; the precise basin requires confirmation.

statement: For equation (1), x'=x exp(alpha(t)−u^2/2−c0 x), u'=(1−s)u−c1 s x, take p-periodic 0<alpha(t)<1, p≥2, c0>0, c1≠0 and 0<s<2. The precise global basin is not established in this index and must be recovered from the cited theorem and its original proof before an attempt.
source_locator: Section 4.1 Conjecture 2; equation (1), equivalently the single-species case of equation (3).
status_basis: The paper states this conjecture beyond its small-perturbation theorem. No later resolution was located in the scoped title/author search. The printed reference to system (3) is retained as a single-species specialization.

title: Bifurcations of the periodically forced evolutionary Ricker model
statement: Determine the bifurcation scenarios of the p-periodic single-species evolutionary Ricker system (1), including loss of stability of its positive periodic orbit as growth-rate and evolution-speed parameters vary. status_basis: An explicit research problem in the 2024 paper; scoped later searches found no comprehensive classification. Specific periods or parameter regions may already be known and need a narrower novelty check.

title: Chemical recurrence for weakly reversible stochastic reaction networks
statement: For every finite weakly reversible reaction network with stochastic mass-action propensities and positive rate constants, is each state of the associated continuous-time count process positive recurrent? Address arbitrary species number, beyond announced two-species results, with well-posedness and nonexplosion explicit. Stoichiometric conservation and communicating classes must be retained.
source_locator: 2020 introduction and section 3; Cappelletti's 2023 two-dimensional talk abstract.
status_basis: The general conjecture is explicit in the paper; the author's later abstract reports a two-species solution. Searches found later two-dimensional announcements, not a general-dimensional theorem.

title: Approximate equilibrium in quitting games with at least four players
statement: Does every finite-player quitting game with at least four players admit an epsilon-Nash equilibrium for every epsilon>0? Each player independently randomizes a quitting time in N∪{infinity}; bounded payoffs depend on the first quitting set, with a specified payoff if nobody quits. External public correlation is not allowed.
source_locator: EMS problem 251*; 2026 APS paper introduction and section 2.
status_basis: The author problem list asks the general existence question. The 2026 paper still limits its characterization to a subset and reports unknown general subgame-perfect existence; it supplies no general resolution of the original question.

title: A finite-energy-density many-body localized phase in the random-field XXZ chain
statement: For the isolated interacting spin-1/2 random-field XXZ chain of equation (7), with independent uniform bounded longitudinal fields and fixed nonzero interaction, determine whether a stable many-body localized phase exists at infinite-temperature energy density for sufficiently strong finite disorder. source_locator: Review sections III.3–III.4 and IV.1 question 2; Elgart–Klein abstract and section 2.3.
status_basis: The review explicitly leaves the phase question unresolved. The July 2026 theorem concerns fixed low-energy intervals, so it does not settle this finite-energy-density formulation.

title: Does failure of thermalization imply local integrals of motion?

The reverse implication is known in the reviewed framework; determine sufficient assumptions for the converse or construct a counterexample satisfying the same definition.
source_locator: Review section IV.1 question 1 and section III.3.
status_basis: The review explicitly asks the converse. The later fixed-energy light-cone theorem does not prove this general equivalence; no resolving source was found in the scoped localization search.

title: Coexistence of eigenstate thermalization and asymptotic subdiffusion
statement: Can an isolated, interacting disordered quantum spin chain with a static Hamiltonian satisfy the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis while exhibiting genuine asymptotic subdiffusive transport, with dynamical exponent z>2, rather than a long finite-time crossover? Use the review's ETH and transport conventions and specify the conserved quantity and limiting procedure.
source_locator: Review section IV.1 question 3 and section VIII; Summer et al. Introduction and finite-size caveats for a later, different model.
status_basis: Explicitly posed in the review. The inspected 2026 circuit paper reports finite-size discrete-time behavior and explicitly limits its thermodynamic claims; it does not resolve this static-Hamiltonian question. A comprehensive search over all model classes remains outstanding.

title: Microscopic validity of avalanche descriptions of the localization transition
statement: For a specified disordered interacting spin-chain Hamiltonian, determine whether thermal-inclusion avalanche dynamics accounts for its putative ETH–MBL transition, and derive a falsifiable quantitative consequence from the microscopic model. The question is conditional on the existence of the relevant transition; a phenomenological avalanche rule alone is not its derivation.
source_locator: Review section IV.1 question 4 and section IX; later fixed-energy theorem.
status_basis: The review identifies the microscopic applicability of avalanche models as unresolved. The inspected 2026 theorem has a different spectral scope and does not settle this mechanism question.

title: Asymptotic saturation of low-Prandtl small-scale dynamos
statement: Determine the nonlinear saturation mechanism and magnetic-to-kinetic energy scaling for statistically forced small-scale MHD dynamos at Pm=nu/eta≪1 as Reynolds numbers become large. Specify forcing and boundaries; the target is asymptotic saturation, not the already demonstrated existence of some low-Pm dynamos.
source_locator: Rincon section 3.5.3; 2025 Taylor–Couette result for contrasting scope.
status_basis: The review identifies saturation as unresolved. Later low-Pm existence results concern particular flows and do not give a universal asymptotic saturation law; the quantitative frontier needs a specialist update.

title: Low-Prandtl transition of the zero-net-flux MRI dynamo
statement: In the unstratified, zero-net-flux, incompressible Keplerian shearing-box model with fixed box aspect ratio and shear-periodic boundaries, determine the dynamo transition boundary Rm_c(Re), especially whether sustained MRI dynamo action survives as Pm=Rm/Re tends to zero. Keep wall-bounded and stratified geometries separate.
source_locator: Rincon section 5.3.4, figure 41; Mishra et al. abstract.
status_basis: The review presents the asymptotic transition alternatives as unresolved. The 2025 low-Pm Taylor–Couette result uses different boundaries and is not a resolution of the specified box limit.

title: A controlled asymptotic bridge from numerical dynamos to Earth's core
statement: For rotating-convection spherical-shell dynamo models, determine whether the strong-field magnetostrophic force balance and associated scaling laws remain valid along physically justified paths toward Earth's very small Ekman and magnetic-Prandtl numbers. Boundary conditions, buoyancy forcing and the asymptotic path must be specified; an MHD limit theorem alone does not identify Earth's actual core regime.
source_locator: Sections 5.1.1–5.1.2, especially Taylor constraint and parameter-gap discussion.
status_basis: The review describes the unresolved extrapolation from accessible simulations to planetary regimes. Scoped later searches found reduced-model and forecasting work, not a general controlled bridge. This remains a broad research-question entry requiring a narrower task.

title: Physical origin of a radiatively stable electroweak hierarchy
statement: What physical mechanism can explain a Higgs/electroweak scale far below higher fundamental scales while controlling radiative sensitivity and satisfying collider constraints? Compare explicit mechanisms using a declared naturalness criterion. Consistency of a technically natural model is a conditional result, not evidence that nature adopts that criterion or mechanism.
status_basis: The source frames electroweak naturalness as unresolved and proposes a conditional model. Searches for later fundamental-physics reviews did not identify an empirically established mechanism.

title: The mechanism that generates neutrino masses and flavor mixing
statement: Which underlying mass-generation mechanism explains the observed nonzero neutrino masses and mixing? Derive distinguishable consequences of specified Dirac, Majorana or seesaw-type models while retaining their additional fields and assumptions. Fitting oscillation parameters does not uniquely identify the mechanism.
source_locator: Rosenlyst introduction problem 2 and section 5; PDG chapter 14.2.
status_basis: Both the named problem and multiple viable mass-model alternatives are documented. No empirical selection among the broad mechanisms is established by the inspected sources.

title: The origin of the cosmic baryon asymmetry
statement: Which physically viable mechanism produced the observed matter–antimatter asymmetry? For explicit baryogenesis or leptogenesis models, connect asymmetry generation, washout and thermal history to independently testable particle or cosmological consequences. A parameter choice reproducing an abundance is not an empirical identification.
status_basis: The source identifies the origin question and supplies one conditional mechanism; it does not establish that mechanism experimentally. Later mechanism proposals do not by themselves close the question.

title: Physical explanation of the small strong-CP parameter
statement: What mechanism explains the exceptionally small effective QCD CP-violating angle while retaining observed quark physics? Compare explicit axion and non-axion mechanisms against radiative stability and empirical constraints. Proving Peccei–Quinn relaxation within its assumed theory does not establish that the theory describes nature.
source_locator: PDG chapter 89.2.1; Rosenlyst introduction problem 6 and section 9.
status_basis: The inspected review states the strong-CP problem and experimental constraints while describing candidate mechanisms. No observed selection of a solution is established.

title: Are the light neutrinos Dirac or Majorana particles?
statement: Determine whether the light neutrino mass eigenstates are Dirac or Majorana, and derive observables that can distinguish these possibilities under specified interactions. In particular, separate statements inferred from a neutrinoless-double-beta-decay mechanism from assumptions about which operator dominates that decay.
source_locator: PDG chapter 14.2 and discussion of neutrinoless double-beta decay.
status_basis: The review retains both mass possibilities and unknown Majorana phases. Oscillation evidence is not sufficient to decide this question; no resolving observation was located in the scoped search.

title: The fundamental composition of non-baryonic dark matter
statement: Identify the fundamental component or components responsible for the non-baryonic dark-matter evidence, through consistent models with discriminating predictions across cosmology, astrophysics and laboratory searches. State gravitational and production assumptions; an allowed parameter point or a relic-density match does not identify the component.
status_basis: The 2025 review explicitly calls the dominant component unknown. Scoped 2026 searches returned model proposals rather than an established identification.

title: The mechanism of late-time cosmic acceleration
statement: Determine whether late-time acceleration is explained by a cosmological constant, evolving dark energy or modified gravitational dynamics, using jointly consistent predictions for expansion and structure growth. Any model-specific reconstruction must declare its gravity, matter-coupling and perturbation assumptions; fitting a background expansion curve alone does not establish the mechanism.
status_basis: The inspected reviews discuss competing explanations and unresolved tensions. Dataset-dependent preferences for evolving dark energy are not a settled physical determination.

title: A jointly consistent explanation of the Hubble tension
statement: Determine whether the discrepancy among early-universe-inferred and late-universe Hubble expansion estimates is explained by observational systematics, modeling assumptions or new physics. A proposed explanation must be assessed jointly against the relevant calibration, CMB, BAO and distance data, with correlations and model dependence explicit.

status_basis: A June 2026 review still evaluates competing explanations. Subsequent searched model papers claim alleviation within assumptions, not a universally established resolution; competing interpretations are retained.

title: The physical origin of primordial inflationary perturbations

status_basis: The sources identify the inflaton/mechanism question and model-dependent inference. Existing constraints support or restrict frameworks without uniquely identifying primordial microphysics.
